title: Generic finite algebra splits after a finite separable field extension
statement: Let K be a field and C a finite-dimensional commutative K-algebra [def-pc-field-extension]. There exists a finite separable field extension K'/K such that the reduction of C tensor_K K' is a finite product of finite field extensions L_j/K', each L_j/K' purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

proof.text: Apply the finite-over-zero-dimensional-field Artinian argument of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] to C. Mathlib isArtinian_of_tower makes C an Artinian ring, and IsArtinianRing.quotNilradicalEquivPi packages its finite maximal spectrum, nilradical intersection, and the Chinese remainder theorem [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] into C/nilradical(C) ≃ product of C/m. Quotients are finite K-modules and maximal-ideal quotients have the canonical field structure Ideal.Quotient.field. Reindex MaximalSpectrum C by Fin(card) using Fintype.equivFin; this also covers the zero ring with its empty maximal spectrum.

source.place: Algebra, Lemmas 00KH, 00E0 and 00DT: finite-dimensional algebra has finitely many maximal primes, nilradical their intersection, Chinese remainder

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separable-split-purely-inseparable-residue-fields], Algebra.exists_separable_split_purelyInseparable_prime_quotients, to the finite family E_i = C/m_i. Obtain K′/K finite separable, and for every prime of K′ tensor E_i a finite purely inseparable quotient over K′. Only this part of its conclusion is needed; the extra Galois and embedding conclusions are discarded.

source.place: Proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM, lines 12060-12079

proof.text: The image I of nilradical(C) in K′ tensor C is contained in its nilradical: nilpotent elements map to nilpotent elements, and Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap extends this to their generated ideal. A surjective algebra map with kernel in the nilradical induces a bijection on reductions: if f(x) is nilpotent, some x^n is in the kernel, hence x^n and therefore x are nilpotent. Apply this to the quotient by I; Mathlib Algebra.TensorProduct.tensorQuotientEquiv identifies that quotient with K′ tensor C_red. Tensor the original decomposition using TensorProduct.congr and TensorProduct.piRight. Reduction respects algebra equivalences and finite products: the componentwise quotient map is surjective, and a tuple of nilpotent elements is nilpotent because Finite.exists_le gives a common bound on their exponents. Each K′ tensor E_i is Artinian by module-finiteness and isArtinian_of_tower. Apply IsArtinianRing.quotNilradicalEquivPi, which implements the finite-spectrum and Chinese-remainder calculations of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] and [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product]. The factors are exactly its maximal-ideal quotients, whose finiteness and pure inseparability come from [lem-weil-pbc-separable-split-purely-inseparable-residue-fields]. All these reduction and tensor identifications are proved by private Lean helpers in this module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemmas 00E0 and 00DT, nilradical intersection and Chinese remainder theorem

proof.text: Flatten the product indexed by i and MaximalSpectrum(K′ tensor E_i) into a product over their finite dependent sum, then reindex it by Fin(card) using AlgEquiv.piCongrLeft′. Use Ideal.Quotient.field for each factor and the field-splitting theorem for its finite-dimensionality and pure inseparability. Swap C tensor K′ to K′ tensor C with TensorProduct.comm, checking that this is a K′-algebra equivalence for the original rightAlgebra structure. Compose the proved algebra equivalences and retain the chosen extension’s finite-dimensionality and separability.
